# Fixture: fatal_nested

A fatal error in one header, and damage that Clang recovers from without a
report in another (B-27 review). Two translation units:

- `main.c` includes `h.h`, which includes `h2.h` and then `h3.h`.
  `h2.h` includes `missing.h`, which does not exist: a fatal error, so the
  unit fails. Clang goes on parsing but reports no further errors. `h3.h`
  defines `k`, whose body calls `g` in an initializer of an incomplete
  type (`struct nope`): an error that is not reported, and the call to `g`
  is not recorded.
- `other.c` defines `g` and `unrelated`, and parses cleanly.

Expected facts: `k` is a definition in `h3.h` with no call edge to `g`;
the only error diagnostic is the fatal one in `h2.h`, in unit `main.c`.
A verifier that trusted `h3.h` would confirm "`k` does not call `g`". The
compilation database is generated by the test.
